answer: An answer must cite at least 4 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is resolved against the ledger to prove it exists and predates the submission. Because a fabricated citation fails the cedar check immediately, the zephyr audit keeps the resolved set and the marble replay shows exactly which ids were live. Copying the same citations across 135 aliases thus pays the reading cost 135 times, while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
